Contradicted by Scientific Evidence

-22% grain fill risk

CLAIM

“Applying common table salt (NaCl) in standing water prevents stem rot in Boro rice.”

Salt increases soil salinity and induces root osmotic shock within 72 hours, hindering grain development rather than controlling stem rot fungi.

Next step: {` Apply 12-15 kg MOP (potassium) at early panicle stage instead.`}

Connect Trishal SAAO

View sources

Supported by Research

Saves 25–30% urea

CLAIM

“Incorporating green mungbean stover into the soil before T. Aman transplanting reduces urea top-dressing.”

Green biomass from BARI Mung-6 decomposes rapidly in warm monsoon soil, providing 35–40 kg natural organic nitrogen per hectare safely without yield

loss.

Next step: {` Incorporate biomass 7–10 days prior to final puddling for optimal nitrogen release.`}

{`Verified for AEZ-9 & AEZ-11`}

View sources

Insufficient Evidence

{`< 8% deterrence observed`}

CLAIM

“Spraying fermented molasses and wood ash solution repels brown planthopper (BPH) effectively.”

Controlled field trials show negligible efficacy against moderate to heavy BPH pressure. Residual leaf sugars may also accelerate secondary Sooty Mold

( Capnodium sp. ).

Next step: {` Install light traps and contact Extension Hotline 16123 for approved bio-pesticide protocols.`}
